Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters View image in fullscreen Fernando Cerimedo in Buenos Aires in 2024. His most recent role was adviser to the Bolivian president, Rodrigo Paz Pereira. Photograph: Agustín Marcarian/Reuters Bolivia Adviser to far-right Latin American leaders arrested for allegedly plotting to kill girlfriend Fernando Cerimedo, 42, arrested on suspicion of ordering shooting of Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller Tiago Rogero South America correspondent Wed 19 Aug 2026 09.44 EDT First published on Wed 19 Aug 2026 09.37 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A senior adviser to many of Latin America’s new wave of far-right leaders has been arrested for allegedly masterminding the attempted murder of his girlfriend. The businessman and political consultant Fernando Cerimedo, 42, had been working as an adviser to the Bolivian president, Rodrigo Paz Pereira, and was one of the main strategists behind Javier Milei’s campaign in Argentina’s 2023 presidential election. He has previously been described as Maga’s man in Latin America – a reference to Donald Trump’s Make America Great Again movement – and is credited with helping secure the US president’s endorsement of the rightwing Nasry “Tito” Asfura , who won Honduras’s presidential election in December. On Tuesday morning, Cerimedo landed in Santa Cruz de la Sierra, in Bolivia, and was arrested before boarding another flight reportedly bound for Buenos Aires , Argentina. According to police, he was detained on suspicion of ordering a gun attack on Nadia Beller, a Bolivian lawyer who local media reported had been in a relationship with Cerimedo – who is married – since last year. View image in fullscreen CCTV footage shows the shooting of Nadia Beller by two men dressed as delivery riders in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. Photograph: Video obtained by Reuters/Reuters Surveillance footage showed two men dressed as delivery riders and wearing helmets open fire on Beller on Monday night outside a hotel in Santa Cruz de la Sierra. She survived and was taken to hospital. Beller told police she had been lured to the hotel after receiving anonymous messages promising to hand over evidence of alleged crimes committed by Bolivia’s leftwing former president Evo Morales , who is subject to two outstanding arrest warrants and remains sheltered in a coca-growing region . Beller said she believed the attack had been a trap orchestrated by Cerimedo. The local police commander, Col David Gómez, told local media that investigators were working on the hypothesis that Beller and Cerimedo had been in a romantic relationship and had had “a personal dispute” in the days before the attack. Cerimedo’s lawyer, Ernesto Giraldes, said his client had not been not trying to flee to Argentina and had travelled to Santa Cruz de la Sierra specifically to visit Beller in hospital, and denied he was behind the attack. View image in fullscreen An evidence marker is placed next to blood stains at a hotel restaurant where Nadia Beller was shot by a man dressed as a delivery rider. Photograph: Ipa Ibanez/Reuters A presidential spokesperson, José Luis Gálvez, said Cerimedo had acted as Paz Pereira’s “personal consultant” but did not hold a government post. The Bolivian president expressed “solidarity” with Beller and posted on X that his administration would offer “zero interference” in the investigation. Cerimedo had a prominent role in Milei’s campaign strategy and had boasted that he had been the one to suggest the self-styled libertarian take a chainsaw to campaign rallies, but he has never held a post in the Argentinian government. In Brazil, Cerimedo was indicted by federal police over his alleged involvement in the attempted coup led by the far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro. In 2022, five days after Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won the election and Bolsonaro refused to concede and plotted ways to remain in power, Cerimedo held a live stream titled “Brazil Was Stolen”, in which he presented an anonymous dossier containing false claims about the vote. Brazil’s federal police later concluded it had been a premeditated operation coordinated with Brazilian military officers and Bolsonaro aides, who had provided Cerimedo with the report. Prosecutors, however, declined to bring charges against him, saying investigators had failed to produce evidence to show Cerimedo knew the report contained fabricated information. Photo: CDC / unsplash.com Sorin Iordan , 28.10.2026, 13:50 The respiratory infection season is in full swing in Romania. According to the National Institute of Public Health (INSP), nearly 82,000 cases of clinical influenza, acute upper respiratory tract infections, and pneumonia were reported during the week of October 12–18, a 0.8% decrease from the previous week and nearly 6% below the figures for the same period last year. The INSP notes that one influenza-related death has been confirmed during the current flu season, which began in October, and over 400,000 people have been vaccinated. Recently, however, the flu vaccine has been unavailable in pharmacies, due to both very high demand and the fact that the World Health Organization determined the composition of the vaccine for this flu season later than usual. The situation has been addressed with the arrival of approximately 370,000 doses of the flu vaccine into distribution warehouses, as announced by the National Agency for Medicines and Medical Devices of Romania. These will be supplemented by another 500,000 doses, expected to arrive in mid-November, to support the ongoing flu vaccination campaign. Last week, the Health Minister Alexandru Rogobete stated that there was a delay in vaccine production across Europe this year, and that Romania was not the only country affected by the shortage. Four influenza vaccines are authorized in Romania: two for adults and two for children, adolescents, and the elderly. According to the National Agency for Medicines, ‘Fluenz’, intended for children and adolescents, and ‘Efluelda’, intended for individuals over 60, have been available in sufficient quantities in pharmacies and through distributors. Issues arose regarding the injectable vaccines for adults, ‘Vaxigrip’ and ‘Influvac’; their stocks had been largely depleted, but they have been replenished. Influenza vaccination is one of the most important measures for preventing the flu and its associated complications, particularly among vulnerable individuals. Doctors recommend vaccination, especially for those over 65, children, individuals with chronic illnesses, pregnant women, and healthcare personnel. 2026 marks the fourth consecutive year that the new influenza vaccination procedure has been in effect. Under this system, vaccine doses are no longer collected from family physicians’ offices; instead, they are obtained from pharmacies, either via a prescription, for those eligible for subsidized vaccines, or without a prescription, at the patient’s own expense. For those not eligible for a subsidized vaccine, a single dose costs approximately 80 lei (about 15 euros). Some pharmacies offer on-site administration of the vaccine. In locations where this service is not available, patients must take the vaccine to their family physician’s office.
